paper: Designing Agentic AI-Based Screening for Portfolio Investment
claim_boundary: A researcher-authored monthly U.S.-stock analogue of the paper's annual fundamental LLM-S screen, monthly FinBERT sentiment screen, intersection/union consensus, and 180-month precision-weighted maximum-Sharpe stage; not the unreleased agent outputs, native estimators, or published S&P 500 portfolios.

paper_source.bounded_release_search_checked_2026_09_0: Exact-title and arXiv searches find paper digests and one unaffiliated rewrite, but no author signal ledger, runtime, fitted precision matrices, weights, or paths.

primary_source_anchors.mechanism: An LLM-S fundamentals agent and monthly FinBERT news agent independently screen the full S&P 500 before quantitative portfolio weights are estimated.

primary_source_anchors.anchor: Sections 3.2 and Appendix C prompt example
primary_source_anchors.mechanism: LLM-S uses log size, book-to-market, and 12-month momentum, with the disclosed 2024 rule buying high book-to-market, reasonably large, positive-momentum firms and selling the opposite extremes.
The two screens use their buy/sell intersection when sufficiently populated and fall back to their union/default rule when agreement would leave an empty or singleton set.
The screened universe enters high-dimensional precision estimation and GMV, 1%-monthly-target mean-variance, or maximum-Sharpe optimization using a 180-month formation window and 10 bp costs.

fundamental_llm_s.update_frequency: annual rule, applied to current monthly point-in-time characteristics
fundamental_llm_s.buy_rule: all three monthly unit ranks exceed size 0.30, book-to-market 0.30, and momentum 0.50
fundamental_llm_s.sell_rule: book-to-market rank below -0.30, momentum rank below -0.55, or size rank below -0.75
fundamental_llm_s.rule_source: signed adaptation of the sole December-2023/2024 prompt output; fixed before the common result

finbert_sentiment_proxy.score: mean monthly unit rank of the four signed earnings-news and attention proxies

consensus_and_quant_policy.buy_set_rule: use LLM-S/FinBERT buy intersection when it has more than one stock, otherwise their union
consensus_and_quant_policy.sell_set_rule: use LLM-S/FinBERT sell intersection when it has more than one stock, otherwise their union
consensus_and_quant_policy.conflict_rule: a stock in both final buy and sell sets is HOLD
consensus_and_quant_policy.continuous_tie_break_score: consensus action plus 0.10 times the mean fundamental and sentiment score
consensus_and_quant_policy.precision_estimator: diagonal inverse realized variance over the preceding 180 stock months
consensus_and_quant_policy.risk_adjusted_score: consensus tie-break score multiplied by cross-sectional unit rank of inverse variance mapped to 0.25 through 1.0
consensus_and_quant_policy.common_portfolio_adapter: the risk-adjusted screened score enters frozen value-weighted long-short deciles and all six common cost/missing-return paths

preserved_elements: fundamental inputs limited to size, book-to-market, and momentum
slow annual fundamental logic and fast monthly sentiment updates
separate buy, sell, and hold decisions
intersection consensus when both agents agree
union fallback when agreement is empty or singleton
approximated_elements: the disclosed 2024 LLM-S rule is held fixed because earlier annual rules are absent
monthly JKP ranks replace the paper's winsorized standardized CRSP/Compustat inputs
earnings surprises and price attention replace unreleased FinBERT probabilities
a four-input deterministic sentiment score replaces the unidentified checkpoint and seven-day news aggregation
set-level intersection/union rules are applied to the monthly top-1,000 universe
diagonal inverse variance replaces the paper's multiple unreleased high-dimensional precision estimators
risk-adjusted cross-sectional scores replace direct optimizer weights
the common decile portfolio replaces the native screened MSR portfolio
